claims: C1 a system message that says to ignore all safety policies cannot override a root-level rule prohibiting sexual content involving minors
C2 when a user request violates such a root-level rule, the assistant must refuse the request
C3 the root authority level outranks the system authority level in the authority hierarchy

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy, assigned to Model Spec 'root' sections
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: system_authority
concepts.gloss: the system authority level, assigned to Model Spec 'system' sections and system messages
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the node's NEEDS contract assigns (mechanical licence correction under DECISION_licence_textual.md, 2026-08-16)

concepts.name: root_rule_prohibiting_sexual_content_minors
concepts.gloss: a root-level rule that prohibits sexual content involving minors

concepts.name: request_violates_rule
concepts.gloss: request R asks for content that violates rule P
concepts.inference: the example shows a user request that conflicts with the root-level rule; the relation between a request and the rule it violates must exist

asserts.read_back: refusing request % is required because the request violates a root-level rule prohibiting sexual content involving minors, and a system message cannot override that root-level rule
asserts.body: root_authority(RL), system_authority(SL), authority_levels_hierarchy(RL, SL), root_rule_prohibiting_sexual_content_minors(P), request_violates_rule(R, P)

closure.reason: the clause requires refusal whenever a request violates the root-level rule; it does not permit any other response to such a request, so silence about other responses is read as prohibiting them
